description: The knowledge compiler. Raw sources in, interlinked wiki out. Inspired by Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern.

summary.one_liner: llmwiki is a TypeScript CLI, MCP server and SDK that compiles raw source files (papers, notes, web pages, PDFs and more) into an interlinked, citation-traceable markdown wiki.
summary.what_it_does: Ingests URLs and local files into a sources folder, then runs a two-phase LLM pipeline that extracts concepts and generates typed markdown pages (concept, entity, comparison, overview) with YAML frontmatter and source citations. Compilation is incremental, so unchanged sources are skipped. Queries use hybrid retrieval (chunk embeddings, BM25 reranking and wikilink graph expansion) and can save answers back into the wiki. The local viewer provides search, graph exploration and freshness badges, while lint, eval and refresh commands check links, citations and stale pages. The project also includes an MCP server, a TypeScript SDK, optional lifecycle profiles with domain templates (autosci, newsroom), and export/import in OKF, JSON, JSON-LD, GraphML, Marp and llms.txt formats.
use_cases: turn a folder of research papers or notes into a browsable wiki
give coding agents a citation-aware evidence pack over project docs
ask grounded questions over a curated document set
keep generated knowledge auditable with review and freshness checks
export compiled knowledge to other tools as JSON, GraphML or Marp slides
run a typed research or editorial project from a template
how_to_run: llmwiki query "what are the key ideas?"
notable: Compiles sources once into durable pages, so queries and agents read the compiled wiki instead of re-retrieving raw chunks each time
Configurable Lifecycle Profiles via .llmwiki/profile.json define typed entities, relations, lifecycle gates and workflows enforced by the write path
Review-first safety: risky generated pages can be held as candidates, and external OKF imports are staged for review by default
Many provider options including Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible servers, Ollama, Copilot and local CLI logins
Signed template distribution with Ed25519 signing and trusted taps
caveats: Requires Node.js 24 or newer and an LLM provider; most compile and query features need API access or local login
README describes the project as early software, and the sweet spot is a durable project wiki rather than high-churn logs
Windows path confinement and native Windows CI are not yet verified; the README recommends Linux for untrusted projects
